pages.notes: Bug0 completeness question explicitly answered No; repeated circling of a concave/trap obstacle despite a reachable goal. No path-optimality conclusion follows.
Bug1 complete loop, closest-to-goal boundary point, then shortest boundary return to that point. Diagram H1/L1/H2/L2 consistent with survey and return.
Bug2 original start–goal line, fixed wall-following side, leave at a closer re-crossing than the hit. Locally free outgoing motion must be supplied for complete operational examples.
Bug2 idealized completeness, conditional practical efficiency, ignored kinematics and sensitivity to latest noisy reading. Do not state unconditional efficiency.
VFH three-stage reduction: occupancy history to polar density to steering chosen over valleys.
Threshold above blocked and below free; equality not stated. Plot extends −180 to +180; circular wrap and equality policy must be explicit in exercises.
Valley is contiguous free run; wide/narrow candidate guidance. Angular span alone is not finite-footprint metric clearance.

Cost equation uses candidate differences from goal/current/previous common reference directions. Weights affect goal aggressiveness and smoothing/reactivity. Candidate error triples must be jointly realizable.
VFH+ masking for reachability/turning limits, turn cost and look-ahead. Supplied numeric mask and candidate policy must not be described as the source’s complete algorithm.

C-space axes are joint angles; red current point lies outside shaded C-obstacle. Forward-kinematics mapping arrow and nonuniform stylized ticks need prior qualifications preserved. One point is not route connectivity.
Local minima can stall away from goal; arm dimensionality, self-collision, dynamics and all-link awareness listed.
CNN example specifically classifies/segments obstacles from camera images. Distinguish perception from depth regression and steering policies; learned cost/threshold adaptation separately listed.
Reward framework shared between mobile and manipulator, but steering/velocity versus joint-angle/torque action spaces differ. No unchanged-policy-transfer guarantee.
Actual summary pixel view confirms repeated A*, Bug, VFH/VFH+ and whole-arm concepts. No unique new formula or premise; mark repeated with earlier-page links and retain qualifications.
